historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly separates media mount from installation but its command has unsafe authentication/TLS and weak host/resource/ISO guards.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds exact BMC/VirtualMedia identity, signed ISO, stable disk target, KVM operator, event policy and media cleanup.

original_test_intent: Mount the approved Linux ISO through the correct BMC virtual-media device, complete installation, reboot successfully and validate system events.
original_method: Agent may securely insert/read/eject the exact VirtualMedia resource after approval; qualified operator selects boot and completes target, partition, package, credential and reboot steps in KVM.
manual_activity: User approves endpoint, ISO, wipe target and recovery; agent may manage exact VirtualMedia state; qualified operator completes KVM boot/install/reboot.
required_inputs: Verified BMC host, manager/VirtualMedia resource IDs and firmware support
Trusted TLS/certificate path and secure credential mechanism
Signed/checksummed authorized ISO URL plus Linux/package baseline
Stable target disk/partition/boot/wipe policy and non-target exclusions
Qualified KVM operator, OOB, backup/recovery and known-event allowlist
safety_requirements: Verify BMC/host/resource and current media/boot state before InsertMedia
Authenticate without inline secrets and validate TLS
Verify ISO integrity and stable target identity before install
Stop on wrong host/media/resource, ambiguous disk, installer/boot/event/BMC fault or recovery loss
Eject or retain media only under explicit final-state policy
agent_execution_scope: Collect post-boot OS/package/storage/health and event evidence
Do not choose boot target, operate installer, enter secrets, partition disks or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve endpoint/resource, ISO, wipe/package/event and recovery policy
Provide qualified operator and own destructive install/recovery
Review media, install, reboot and event evidence to decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Redfish InsertMedia fits media mounting, but inline secrets, TLS bypass and unverified resource/host are unsafe; lsblk alone does not prove correct VirtualMedia or installation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the pinned vendor-supported API with secure auth/TLS against the exact resource, verify Image and Inserted state, then perform policy-controlled eject after operator installation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC ISO mount, Linux all-package install, event review, reboot workability and source 5/30 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat insert/status, KVM install and final eject as distinct evidence phases bound to one verified host, ISO and target disk.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds secure management identity and destructive target guards without automating interactive installation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: VirtualMedia control may be automated; installer and physical-impact decisions remain manual.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: BMC implementations vary in resource IDs, boot override semantics, transfer protocol and media persistence.

project_override_considerations: Only the project-approved BMC API, resource IDs, TLS trust, ISO server and boot-override method may be used; generic Managers/1/VirtualMedia/CD assumptions are prohibited.
expected_evidence: Critical approval and verified BMC/host/resource/TLS identity
Operator KVM boot/install/partition/reboot screenshots and logs
Complete OS events/BMC SEL, known-event triage, final eject state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define BMC-mounted ISO installation and post-reboot/event acceptance.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Verified BMC interface, ISO, target policy, operator and recovery are supplyable prerequisites; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Separates secure VirtualMedia automation from manual destructive installer control and closes endpoint, secret, TLS, target and cleanup gaps.
independent_technical_reasoning: A successful HTTP response can come from the wrong BMC or virtual-media resource and does not prove the next boot or installer disk. Evidence must bind BMC identity, returned Image/Inserted state, KVM boot selection and stable target serial across the destructive install, with explicit media cleanup to avoid unintended future boots.
